pages.hook: In the USA, “What do you do?” is one of the first questions at a party. It means “What is your job?” and people expect a short answer.

mythfact.s: “What do you do?” asks about your job.
mythfact.why: It is a common small-talk question, not “What are you doing now?”

mythfact.s: Brooklyn is a separate city outside New York.
mythfact.why: Brooklyn is one of the five boroughs of New York City.

mythfact.s: The Brooklyn Bridge opened in 1883.
mythfact.why: It connects Brooklyn and Manhattan and opened in 1883.

mythfact.s: Restaurant servers in the USA usually get tips.
mythfact.why: Tips are a big part of their income, so 15 to 20 percent is normal.

mythfact.s: You say “I am teacher” in English.
mythfact.why: Use a: “I’m a teacher.”

decode.q: What jobs does the restaurant need?
decode.why: The sign lists Cook, Server and Driver.

compare.br: In Brazil, people often ask first about your family, your city or your team (time) before your job.
compare.us: In the USA, people often ask about your job early. It is a way to start a chat, not to judge.
compare.tip: Say your job and add one more detail: “I’m a teacher. I love my students.”
compare.ask: What do you do? Say it in English, with one more detail.

quiz.q: To say your job, you say…
“Do you like your job?” — a short answer is…
Where is the restaurant? “On Fifth Avenue.” What does “on” show here?

pages.polite: After someone says their job, ask **“Do you like it?”** It shows interest and keeps the chat friendly.

Reading quest — A teacher and a cook in Brooklyn · part 1
text: Brooklyn is a big part of New York City. Many people live and work there. Two neighbors, Maria and Ava, talk on the stairs. “**What do you do, Maria?**” asks Ava. “**I’m a teacher**,” says Maria. “**And you?**”
“**I’m a cook**,” says Ava. “**I work in a restaurant.**” Maria says, “Cool! **Do you like your job?**” “**Yes, I do. It’s busy but fun**,” Ava says. She works long hours, so she is tired at night.
“**Where is the restaurant?**” asks Maria. “**On Fifth Avenue**,” says Ava. “**Come for lunch!**” Maria answers, “**I will!** Thanks.” Ava says, “**See you at lunch!**”

opts: Two neighbors talk about their jobs
fast.why: Maria and Ava talk about their jobs.

Ava works in a restaurant. Maria is a teacher.
“Yes, I do. It’s busy but fun.”

tf.s: Busytown is a real city in Brooklyn.
tf.why: It is a town in a book.

order: Ava asks Maria about her job.
Maria says she is a teacher.
Ava says she is a cook.
Maria asks about the restaurant.
Ava invites her for lunch.

ctx.why: Busy = with a lot of work.

ctx.sent: She works long hours, so she is tired.

pages.title: Reading quest — A teacher and a cook in Brooklyn · part 2
text: There is a famous book about jobs. In 1968, Richard Scarry made “What Do People Do All Day?” It shows Busytown, where everyone has a job. The farmer grows food, the builder makes houses, and the mechanic fixes cars. In the book, each job helps the town.

This is true in real life too. A teacher helps children learn. A cook makes food for hungry people. A driver takes people home. When you ask “What do you do?”, you learn how a person helps their town.

unscramble.ans: Cool! Do you like your job?
unscramble.pt: Legal! Você gosta do seu trabalho?

speed.q: Complete a fala: “So, ____?” (E aí, qual é o seu trampo?)
speed.why: “what's your gig” = qual é o seu trampo

speed.q: Complete a fala: “Yeah, ____ every night.” (É, fico exausto toda noite.)
Complete a fala: “I'm a cook. It's a lot, but I ____.” (Sou cozinheiro. É muita coisa, mas eu adoro.)

opts: Oi! Sou o Omar. Tenho vinte e cinco anos.
Na Joe's Pizza, perto do parque.
Valeu, está com um cheiro ótimo!

dict.say: Yes, I do. It's busy but fun.

errors.wrong: I work in the Fifth Avenue.
errors.why: Use on + street name, with no the.

errors.alt: He is work in a restaurant.

pages.title: Boss mission — What do you do?

brief.teacher: You are Ava. Change the plan during the scene.
brief.student: You meet Ava, a neighbor, in Brooklyn. Talk about jobs. You are the customer / visitor.

orders: What do you do? I work as an engineer.
complications: The other person did not hear you: repeat.

pages.title: Free production
pages.prompt: Você conhece alguém numa festa. Pergunte o que a pessoa faz e diga o que você e outra pessoa fazem, com work as. Ligue à referência What Do People Do All Day?: é o livro das profissões numa cidade: What do you do?.
pages.model: What do you do? I work as a manager. My sister works as an actor. What Do People Do All Day? helps here.

tasks.name: Say it
tasks.prompt: O que você faz? Eu trabalho como engenheiro.
tasks.model: What do you do? I work as an engineer.

items: Record 30 seconds: “I’m a… I work in…”
